claim_type_rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined after two upstream anchors: (a) the 18-group universe is anchored by Wikipedia's `Group (periodic table)` article (which explicitly lists 18 IUPAC-numbered groups and notes the 14 f-block columns are unnumbered); (b) row-membership is anchored by the master `Periodic table` article (IUPAC group-membership), which assigns every numbered-group element to a single group including Hydrogen in Group 1. The ranking rule 'three lowest atomic numbers per group' is a total ordering on a closed set — no curator judgment after these anchors. This is distinct from `candidate_rebuild` (which would require curator-bounded universe selection) and distinct from `partially_supplemented` (no rebuilding of the master subset). The cycle-1 design audit confirmed `source_defined` becomes defensible AFTER renaming away from the 'representative elements' framing (which would have implied curator-judgment selection); the staged form uses 'lowest three atomic numbers' which is purely source-defined.

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (cycle-0 source exploration + audit-cycle-1 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS + audit-cycle-2 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS) produced a source-faithful instance. Cycle-0 verified the existence of the master `Group (periodic table)` article + 18 per-group articles. Audit-cycle-1 issued 6 amendments most-load-bearing of which was switching the universe source from chemical-family pages (Alkali metal, Halogen, Noble gas) to the master IUPAC periodic-table source (fixing the Hydrogen anomaly so H is included in Group 1) + renaming away from the misleading 'representative elements' framing to 'first three elements by atomic number' (which is deterministic and source-defined). Audit-cycle-2 issued 2 more amendments: explicit numeric-group-order sort contract (parse integer from 'Group N' string, NOT lexicographic) + reword per-group articles to clarify their role is validation (not uniform validators of row membership) with Group 1 specifically called out as non-uniform (the Alkali metal article doesn't include H). Cycle-1 post-staging audit then required the source-roles to use canonical artifact-contract vocab (universe / ranking / value / validation / entity-detail) and the 18 per-group URLs to live in provenance prose rather than registered source_urls. All amendments incorporated; the staged design is locked.
collection_summary.partition_structure: 18 IUPAC-numbered groups × 3 lowest-atomic-number elements per group = 54 rows. Composite PK (Group, Element). Each group's partition has exactly 3 rows.
collection_summary.row_count_check: 18 × 3 = 54 rows. Each group has exactly 3 elements per the lowest-atomic-number rule (every numbered group has at least 3 members — Group 3 has 4: Sc, Y, Lu, Lr; other groups have 4-7). No partition is short.

roles.role_note: universe: assigns every numbered-group element to its single IUPAC group (1 through 18), including Hydrogen in Group 1; row-membership for the staged set. value: supplies Element name, Symbol, and Atomic Number cell values for all 54 staged rows.

universe: defines the 18-numbered-group set and the unnumbered f-block (lanthanides + actinides) exclusion. Also documents alternative naming conventions (IUPAC, Mendeleev, CAS, Old IUPAC, trivial names) — used during curation for cross-reference but does not carry a value role for any cell.

validation_cross_checks.rationale: Per artifact-contract.md: validation sources do not count toward source_count and live in source_coverage_notes prose rather than registered source_urls. The 18 per-group Wikipedia articles below were consulted during curation as validation sources for each group's element enumeration. They are documented here for provenance transparency. None of them carry a universe or value role for the staged set; the universe role is carried by the 2 masters above (Periodic_table + Group_(periodic_table)) and the value role is carried by Periodic_table.
validation_cross_checks.non_uniform_validation_case: Group 1 — Wikipedia's Alkali metal article enumerates Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr as the alkali-metal chemical family and notes separately that 'together with hydrogen they constitute group 1'. It does NOT include H in its alkali-metal enumeration. Under the chemical-family framing, Group 1 = Li, Na, K (excludes H). Under the IUPAC group-membership framing (which this instance uses, anchored by the master Periodic table), Group 1 = H, Li, Na (includes H). The Alkali metal article validates the Li/Na members but is non-uniform on H. All other 17 per-group articles are uniform with their respective IUPAC group-membership.

decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1, AFTER renaming from 'representative elements')
decision_log.rationale: The pre-cycle-1 framing 'representative elements' would have required curator-judgment selection (which 3 of each group's N members are 'representative'?), which would have made `source_defined` overclaim what the sources provide. Audit-cycle-1 amendment #1 renamed to 'first three elements by atomic number' — a deterministic total-ordering rule grounded in atomic number (a fixed source-defined property). With this rename, `source_defined` is defensible: the master `Group (periodic table)` defines 18 groups; the master `Periodic table` assigns each element to its IUPAC group; the lowest-3-atomic-numbers rule is a deterministic ordering. No curator judgment after the universe + ranking-rule anchors.

decision_log.decision: Universe source = master Periodic table + Group (periodic table); per-group chemical-family pages serve a validation role only
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #2 + audit-cycle-2 amendment #2: chemical-family pages (Alkali metal, Halogen, Noble gas, Pnictogen, Chalcogen, Carbon group, Boron group) define chemical families which can differ from IUPAC numbered groups. The Hydrogen issue is the canonical example: the Alkali metal article excludes H from its chemical-family enumeration while the IUPAC periodic table includes H in Group 1. To honor the title's 'IUPAC-numbered periodic table groups' framing, the universe role is carried by the master Periodic table (IUPAC group-membership). The 18 per-group articles serve a validation role; Group 1's Alkali metal article is specifically non-uniform with respect to IUPAC group-membership and is documented as such.

decision_log.decision: Hydrogen IS in Group 1's staged set (H, Li, Na — lowest 3 atomic numbers in Group 1)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #2 resolution: under the IUPAC group-membership framing (the universe source — Periodic_table), Hydrogen is in Group 1. Top 3 by lowest atomic number = H (1), Li (3), Na (11). The alternative under the chemical-family framing (Alkali metal article — which has a validation role only) would have given Li, Na, K (top 3 alkali metals, excluding H), but this would conflict with the title's 'IUPAC-numbered groups' framing. The staged set follows IUPAC; the chemical-family framing is documented as the rejected alternative in source_coverage_notes::validation_cross_checks::non_uniform_validation_case for Group 1.

decision_log.decision: Group 3 framing = IUPAC 2021 ruling (Sc, Y, Lu, Lr); top 3 = Sc, Y, Lu
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4: the current Wikipedia `Group 3 element` article uses the IUPAC 2021 ruling Sc-Y-Lu-Lr. The historical La/Ac framing (Sc-Y-La-Ac) is documented in the same article as a competing alternative that 'most authors focusing on the subject are against' (per the Wikipedia article). The IUPAC 2021 ruling was reaffirmed by IUPAC. The staged Group 3 = Sc (21), Y (39), Lu (71). The historical La (57) + Ac (89) framing — if used — would have given Sc, Y, La. The staged form follows the current Wikipedia + IUPAC ruling.

decision_log.decision: Lanthanides + actinides (f-block) are out of scope
decision_log.rationale: Per master `Group (periodic table)` article: 'there are 18 numbered groups in the periodic table; the 14 f-block columns are not numbered.' Lanthanides + actinides are unnumbered f-block columns, not numbered groups. The title explicitly scopes to 'the 18 IUPAC-numbered periodic table groups'. f-block elements are out of scope; this is honest scope-narrowing, not exclusion of in-scope rows.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (Group, Element, Symbol, Atomic Number); composite PK (Group, Element)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #5: Atomic Number earns its column because it is the ranking attribute that defines the row-selection rule (lowest 3 atomic numbers per group). Alternative: replace Atomic Number with State at STP — REJECTED in cycle-1 because it would shift the instance from a clean deterministic decomposition into a mixed projection. Alternative: drop Atomic Number, keep 3 cols (Group + Element + Symbol) — REJECTED because the ranking attribute would no longer be in the staged table. Composite PK (Group, Element) matches the precedent set by `apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews` (Mission, Astronaut) + `foundational_painters_of_major_modern_art_movements` (Movement, Painter).

decision_log.decision: Sort = numeric group-number ASC primary, Atomic Number ASC secondary (NOT lexicographic Group ASC)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit-cycle-2 amendment #1 (BLOCKING / structural): Group is a string field 'Group 1' through 'Group 18'. Plain lexicographic sort would give 'Group 1, Group 10, ..., Group 18, Group 2, Group 3, ...' — incorrect. The sort contract is explicit: parse the integer from 'Group N' string and sort numerically. The db_analog uses `g.group_number ASC` (numeric column in the relational analog). The staged CSV uses numeric-parsed ordering: Group 1, Group 2, ..., Group 18. Within each group, Atomic Number ASC.

Per audit-cycle-1 amendment #6: the PK 'Group N' is a conceptual category (an IUPAC numbering scheme), not an individual chemical entity. The abstract-categories bucket is more semantically consistent than taxonomic-entities (which contains moons, species, nutrients — individual physical entities). Abstract-categories bucket: religions×2, languages, philosophical-schools, architectural-styles, + chemical-groups (NEW) = 6 instances after this Ready. The Element column (composite PK 2) is an individual chemical entity, but the partitioning Group field is the categorical scaffolding.

normalization_decisions.rule: String form 'Group N' where N is the IUPAC group number (1 through 18). Per audit-cycle-2 amendment #1: sort contract is explicit numeric-parse from 'Group N' string, NOT lexicographic. Numeric range 1-18; no leading-zero padding (use 'Group 1' not 'Group 01').

Capitalized English name per Wikipedia article title (e.g., 'Hydrogen', 'Lithium', 'Aluminium'). IUPAC spellings preserved: 'Aluminium' (NOT American 'Aluminum'), 'Sulfur' (NOT British 'Sulphur') — Wikipedia uses IUPAC spellings as article titles.
1-2 letter chemical symbol per IUPAC standard. First letter capitalized, second (if any) lowercase. Examples: 'H', 'Li', 'Na', 'Ca', 'Hg'. Universal across all chemistry sources.
Integer (Z) per IUPAC standard. 1 through 80 in the staged set (lowest H=1 to highest Hg=80 among the 54 staged rows). Universal across all chemistry sources.

open_questions.question: Should the historical Group 3 framing (Sc, Y, La, Ac) be acknowledged in the staged set or only in decision_log?
open_questions.answer: Only in decision_log. The staged Group 3 = Sc, Y, Lu per IUPAC 2021 ruling (consistent with the current `Group_3_element` Wikipedia article). The historical La/Ac framing is the rejected alternative — a documented decision_log entry, not a staged row. If audit prefers the historical framing, swap Lu (71) → La (57) for Group 3's 3rd row.

open_questions.question: Should Roentgenium / Copernicium / other transactinides be in the staged set as Group N's 4th member if a lower-atomic-number Period 7 element doesn't exist?
open_questions.answer: No — the staged rule is 'three lowest atomic numbers per group'. Every numbered group has at least 3 stable/long-lived members in Period 4-6, so the rule never reaches transactinides. The staged set's highest atomic number is Hg=80 (Group 12, Period 6). Transactinides (Period 7, Z>104) are in scope of the master periodic table but not in any group's top-3 by atomic number. No edge case here.
